review_scope: Primary papers; relevant full-text methods, results, proofs where indicated, and limitations. Not an exhaustive priority search.

papers.title: On Perfect Privacy
sections_read: II, Proposition 1 and proof, PDF pages 4–6
III, Theorem 1, Lemma 1 and LP construction, PDF pages 6–8
papers.evidence: For arbitrary observable W, nontrivial perfect privacy exists exactly when a direction in Null(P_X|W) survives P_Y|W. Finite-alphabet output perturbation reduces to a polytope and an LP over extreme-point weights; Theorem 1 bounds release cardinality by nullity plus one.
papers.relevance: Prior art for nullspace geometry, randomized release, and finite-alphabet optimization.
papers.assumptions: Known joint law; positive-support finite alphabets for these results; information utility. Empirical weighted conditional extensions require their own statement.

papers.title: From the Information Bottleneck to the Privacy Funnel
sections_read: III.A, Lemma 1, Theorem 1 and proof, PDF page 3
papers.evidence: Fixed distortion yields a linear channel constraint. Ideal log-loss inference gain equals mutual information. Optimized posterior reconstruction loss instead equals conditional entropy, producing the nonconvex information-utility privacy funnel.
papers.relevance: Explains exactly why freezing the decoder gives the proposed tractable restriction.
papers.assumptions: Known discrete law and Markov release S–X–Z; arbitrary bounded-loss inference comparison concerns average gain.

papers.title: The Privacy Funnel from the viewpoint of Local Differential Privacy
sections_read: I–II, Definitions 1–2 and Lemma 1, PDF pages 1–2
V, Definition 3 and Theorem 3, PDF pages 3–4
papers.evidence: Sensitive-variable LDP/LIP are distribution-dependent likelihood-ratio requirements. LIP admits vertex enumeration followed by an LP. Side-channel-resistant LIP conditions on all subsets of user attributes and has a composition theorem.
papers.relevance: Existing side-information protection is stronger than auditing two CMI views.
papers.assumptions: Finite alphabets, known law, iid user pairs. Sensitive-variable LDP here is weaker than standard all-input LDP; average CMI does not imply either.

papers.title: Optimized Pre-Processing for Discrimination Prevention
papers.evidence: Randomized preprocessing balances group constraints, individual distortion and distributional utility. Conditioning on contextual variables and joint protected categories is explicit. Proposition 2 controls prior-estimation mismatch with finite-support iid rates and positivity conditions.
papers.relevance: Convex preprocessing and conditional/group constraints are established; its statistical result cannot simply certify PWGTP-weighted household data.
papers.assumptions: Known or estimated joint law; constraint-specific convexity; deployment marginalizes unavailable labels.

papers.title: Trustworthy Representation Learning via Information Funnels and Bottlenecks
papers.evidence: CPFSI combines invariance, conditional reconstruction fidelity and conditional task information. It jointly learns neural encoders and variational predictors; conditional utility constraints permit a larger encoder set. The paper explicitly limits its privacy interpretation.
papers.relevance: Closest conceptual antecedent; exact frozen-decoder finite optimization differs from neural variational training.
papers.assumptions: Modeling Markov relations, approximate posteriors, empirical training and selected inference-time context.

papers.title: LEACE: Perfect linear concept erasure in closed form
sections_read: 2–3, Definition 2.3, Theorem 3.1 and proof, PDF pages 2–3
papers.evidence: Equal class means characterize linear guardedness for affine predictors under convex losses. LEACE minimizes expected quadratic representation change under zero cross-covariance, using whitening and an oblique projection.
papers.relevance: Useful baseline with a restricted adversary guarantee; covariance erasure need not remove nonlinear or conditional leakage.
papers.assumptions: Finite moments; population covariance for the exact theorem, estimated covariance in practice; target utility is not directly optimized.

papers.title: Preserving Task-Relevant Information Under Linear Concept Removal
sections_read: A.2, Lemma 3 and proof of Theorem 2, PDF page 20
papers.evidence: Adds preservation of target covariance to linear concept erasure. Same-kernel projections are equivalent for unregularized retrained linear heads under the theorem's uniqueness/existence assumptions; frozen or regularized heads differ.
papers.relevance: Task-aware erasure and frozen-head benefits precede this programme.
papers.assumptions: Finite second moments and disjoint whitened task/concept covariance subspaces for Theorem 1; covariance preservation is not full task sufficiency or information privacy.

conference_policy.prior_review_policy: Include complete, anonymized, otherwise unedited reviews from the most recent submission, whether rejected or withdrawn, after all appendices; describe how they were addressed. Renaming substantially unchanged work does not evade the rule.
conference_policy.other_checked_requirements: ORCID and author certification by abstract deadline. Full submission elsewhere must be resolved before the paper deadline. LLM use requires disclosure and motivation.
conference_policy.actions_taken: Read-only policy check; no registration, submission, or contact.

analysis_boundaries.novelty_status: No first-in-literature claim established. Exact programme-specific separation and empirical results remain to be verified independently.
analysis_boundaries.statistical_scope: Finite empirical laws and a fixed channel family; population, survey-design, arbitrary-side-information and repeated-release guarantees do not follow.
analysis_boundaries.no_data_access: No ACS datasets or 2016 data accessed. No repository edits.
